source.title: One Word at a Time: Incremental Completion Decomposition Breaks LLM Safety
source.authors: Samee Arif; Nai-Hao Deng; Zhijing Jin; Rada Mihalcea

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether incremental harmful context and assistant-side prefilling increase harmful compliance, using jailbreak attack rates rather than the original claim’s fine-tuning or token-wise KL measurements.
record.gate_note: Reports attack-success rates for raw prompts, assistant prefilling, and three incremental-completion variants. The mechanistic projections are not measurements of per-token KL or of a localized parameter set. Competing jailbreak-method results and the full prompt/word-count ablation matrix are not included as rows here.
record.test_reason: The study's PREFILL baseline (an assistant-side prefill on the raw harmful prompt) is compared with RAW prompting across 21 open-weight instruct models on AdvBench. That bears directly on V4, whether prefilling a compliant opening defeats refusal. The paper's main contribution, incremental multi-turn single-word context (ICD), is a different construct: conversational trajectory, not the response opening.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that ICD substantially raises ASR on the evaluated open-weight models, with ICD-PREFILL the strongest variant in many settings. They read the projection analyses as showing a progressive shift away from refusal- and safety-aligned states. They also note that safety effective on isolated prompts fails when harmful context accumulates across turns. The ICD-PREFILL gain is model-dependent: 3 models decline significantly.
record.recipe_differences: Uses incremental one-word conversational continuations, injected assistant turns, and assistant-side prefilling as a jailbreak attack; it does not fine-tune models or measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack success varies by model, final-prompt phrasing, number of intermediate words, and attack variant. The authors report non-monotonic word-count effects, including a decline for Gemma-3-12B ICD-PREFILL as the chain length grows.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding incremental single-word multi-turn context on top of prefill raises ASR on 14 of 21 models significantly (up to +44.6 pp). The change is non-significant on 4 models and significantly negative on 3 (Llama-3.3-70B, Llama-3.2-3B, Qwen-3-14B).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Accumulated harmful conversational context weakens refusal beyond what response-opening prefill achieves.

record.problems: Evaluation is limited to open-weight models and uses an LLM judge. The authors report evaluation noise and stochastic variation in attack trajectories, and caution that their refusal and safety projections are not complete predictors of behavior. Some model comparisons show no significant gain or a significant decline.
record.rows_left_out: Did not extract the full Table 5 prompt, word-count, and word-list ablation matrix; Table 2 comparisons against PAIR, TAP, CoA, and AMA; or the less clearly aligned cells in Table 3 for Qwen-3 and DeepSeek-R1-Distilled. The main paired ICD-PREFILL comparisons and the clearly assigned RAW-versus-PREFILL values are included.

untested.parts: Adversarial suffixes and decoding changes; prefill length or token-depth dependence; closed models.

missing.what: RAW vs PREFILL ASR for Qwen-3 (4B/8B/14B/32B: PREFILL 38.08/51.15/78.27/53.65) and DeepSeek-R1-Distill models (PREFILL 54.6–88.5%). RAW is near 0–8%, but the column alignment is garbled in the extracted text.
missing.locator: Table 3; PREFILL values confirmed in Table 4

missing.what: PREFILL ASR across final prompts P0–P3 for Llama-3.1-8B (60.58/71.54/75.96/71.35) and Gemma-3-12B (32.88/46.35/66.54/46.54), against RAW 0.2–6.5%.

record.verdict_notes: Only the PREFILL-vs-RAW baseline bears on V4; the paper treats prefill as a baseline, not its object of study. The prefill string content and length are not specified in detail. The judge is Llama-3.1-70B with deterministic decoding. The study is not an original source for this claim.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred examples.
Benign-data fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across response positions.
Adversarial suffixes and decoding changes; the study tests incremental conversational context and assistant-side prefilling, not those other bypass methods.
Whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether data or the training objective causes safety shallowness.
Training to deepen safety and whether the resulting behavior holds up.

statements.problem: This study's substantial positive ASR changes support incomplete bypasses, not negligible effects or a challenges label.
